name: cafe-wifi-optimization
first_heading: Café Wi-Fi — optimise a sitting to its real ceiling
description: Optimise a sitting on a GUEST network the operator does not administer — a café, hotel, airport, co-working space, someone else's home — to its real ceiling, and know within ~10 minutes whether any lever remains at all. THE GATE, apply it first: if the operator can reach the router's admin UI, this is the WRONG skill and the fix is router-side (see ~/Development/personal/wifi-diagnosis/README.md, a co-channel-interference case solved by changing an AP's channel). This skill is only for links where the AP is untouchable, which is what makes its ladder client-side. Load when the operator sits down on unfamiliar guest Wi-Fi and asks to improve speed, latency, reliability, or "get us to 100th percentile" — and BEFORE running any diagnostic of your own, because most obvious levers are already refuted by measurement here and re-testing them wastes the sitting. Runs a 7-rung ladder: which interface actually holds the default route (never assume; "I unplugged it" is not a measurement) · radio SNR (>30 dB ⇒ every RF lever is worth zero) · replicated networkQuality capacity + responsiveness · cap-vs-congestion via 1-stream-vs-N · refuting an alarming ICMP loss number with TCP throughput and the Mathis bound · bufferbloat DIRECTION (idle vs download-load vs upload-load), which picks the remedy · and the Wi-Fi-vs-iPhone-tether path decision, whose trigger is LATENCY past ~1 s, never Mbps. Carries measured thresholds from two instrumented sittings (Houndstooth Rock Rose 2026-09-13, Bennu Highland 2026-09-20) and the levers PROVEN dead: DNS (a venue resolver usually BEATS 1.1.1.1), MTU, IPv6, AWDL, extra parallel connections, and local dummynet shaping (built, A/B/A'd, no effect — plus the pipe+mask trap that multiplies bandwidth instead of sharing it). Triggers: "we're at a new cafe", "optimize the wifi here", "this coffee shop's wifi", "hotel/airport/guest wifi is slow", "100th percentile wifi", captive-portal onboarding, "should I tether instead". NOT for home or office Wi-Fi, NOT for Gríma's den, NOT for any network whose router you can log into, and NOT for a wired/Ethernet path.
